Coordinate occupations are independent Bernoulli sin²(t/2^{k+1}), supported on finite subsets because probabilities summable. Viète cosine product yields the singleton expression, interpreted by continuous limits at apparent poles. At t=pi·2^m the lower coordinates vanish, m is certain, and the upper tail has probabilities sin²(pi/2^{j+1}), giving empty tail 4/pi². After h=2^-m, y=ht/2, finite duplication identity localizes all large-m maxima to y=pi/2; near t=pi/h+delta the exact expression has logarithm -2h delta/pi-delta²/3+O(h²delta²+|h delta|³+delta⁴), strict negative second derivative. Stationarity gives unique delta=-3h/pi+O(h³), and gain 3h²/pi²+O(h⁴). Derivative at resonance -2h/pi<0 proves strict improvement for every finite m; probability one would require all infinite upper sin factors zero and hence t=0, impossible. Independent product cross-checks (42 cases) and numerical local maxima m=4..9 support but cannot prove the global optimization.
